A. Introduction and First Reading of an Ordinance Adopting the Fire Hazard Severity Zone Map
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines and adopt a finding of categorical exemptions pursuant to Section 15307 and Section 15308 of the CEQA Guidelines ; and
2. Introduce for first reading an ordinance to add chapter 8.46 to the Santa Monica Municipal Code to designate Fire Hazard Severity Zones as pursuant to California Government Code Section 51178.

C. Approval of Donation of Retired Buses to Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
R ecommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council :
1. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effects pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines; and
2. A uthorize the City Manager to negotiate and execute a Memorandum of Understanding with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LA Metro) for donation of decommissioned transit buses in support of the LA28 Olympic Games. This recommended award is made as an exception to the competitive bidding process as LA Metro has requested donations of decommissioned transit buses for use in the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic games .

F. Adoption of a Resolution Rescheduling Regular City Council Meetings Scheduled for July 22nd to July 29th, September 23rd to September 30th, and Cancelling August 26th and November 25th Council Meetings
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council approve the following:
1. Reschedule regular Council meeting scheduled for July 22, 2025, to July 29, 2025;
2. Cancel the regular Council meeting s scheduled for August 26, 2025 and November 25, 2025 , for summer recess and the Thanksgiving holiday, and due to a lack of quorum;
3. Reschedule regular Council meeting scheduled for September 23, 2025, to September 30, 2025, in observance of Rosh Hashanah;
4. Adopt attached amended resolution approving changes to the regular Council meeting schedule; and
5. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant environmental effects pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines

B. Large Format Digital Signage Study Session
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding that this study session is not a project subject to the California Environmental Quality Act;
2. Authorize City staff to initiate negotiations with the applicant for the Development Agreements for new outdoor digital displays located at 301 Arizona Avenue and 1202 Third Street Promenade ;
3. Provide direction to Staff regarding desired project parameters and approach to community benefits; a nd
4. Discuss the approach for future large-format digital signage with off-site advertising, including the adoption of an ordinance to establish a pilot program to limit this signage to the Third Street Promenade area .

A. Public Hearing and Adoption of a Resolution Establishing Scheduled Five-Year Water Service Rate Adjustments
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Hold a public hearing for the proposed five-year water rate adjustment ;
2. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15273 of the CEQA Guidelines for the five-year water rate adjustment public hearing ;
3. Receive public comments pursuant to Proposition 218 requirement s ;
4. Consider all protests against the proposed water rate adjustments that have been submitted in accordance with Proposition 218 ; and
5. Adopt the resolution establishing five-year schedule of water rate adjustments to go into effect July 1, 2025.

B. Request for Pilot Program Allowing Market-Rate Housing Projects
Request of Councilmember Zwick, Mayor Pro Tem Torosis, and Mayor Negrete that the City Council direct the City Manager to return with a pilot program allowing market-rate housing projects more flexibility in how they provide affordable housing units off-site as a means to incentivize housing production for approved projects that are unable to proceed due to economic uncertainty. The pilot program should include provisions to ensure that the off-site affordable housing units are constructed and also allow housing projects to be eligible for density bonus, incentives/concessions, and modifications under State density bonus law.
